n_demand: 75 kg N/feddan recommended by the agriculture ministry; farmers use about 102
soil_effect: Takes N from the soil. A legume before it helps: fahl berseem after maize raised available soil N, wheat yield and net income in an ARC trial in Sharkia (2023).
pest_notes: Rusts are airborne, so rotation does not control them: leaf rust is common, yellow-rust epidemics hit in 1995/97/99, stem rust Ug99 was detected in Egypt in 2014. More N raised yellow-rust severity in trials.
rotation_hint: Avoid a winter cereal and a summer cereal on the same land back to back (a Springer chapter suggests fahl clover between rice and wheat).
price_card: Gov. price EGP 2,500/ardeb (150 kg), 2026 harvest; 2,650 planned for 2027. Yield 20 ardeb/feddan (minister, Nov 2026). Cost about 50,000/feddan (one union head).

sow_window: Mid-May to early June in Delta trials (15 May-15 Jun at Sakha; 5 May-3 Jun elsewhere); matures in about 122-134 days from planting; USDA says grown May-August
allowed_in_monufia: yes (no restriction found). MINOR crop: about 30,000 ha in all of Egypt (USDA FAS 2026), grown mainly in Middle and Upper Egypt; no Monufia area found. Check seed and buyer before recommending.
egypt_literature_mm: 595-714 (2500-3000 m3/fed applied water, typical Egyptian season)
n_effect: legume: fixes N (but the seed takes most of the N it fixes)
n_demand: about 15 kg N/feddan starter plus Rhizobium seed inoculation (Egyptian wheat-soybean trial); 36 kg N/ha (about 15 kg N/feddan) in a Gharbia trial
soil_effect: In one Egyptian trial with three previous crops (cotton, soybean, maize) the best wheat yield came after soybean, and Egyptian papers call soybean a good break crop. But soybean removes most of the N it fixes in its seed, leaving little residual N. No kg N credit is claimed.
pest_notes: Sucking pests: whitefly (the most abundant in a Kafr El-Sheikh study, peak mid-June to August), spider mites, aphids, leafhoppers; cotton leafworm also attacks soybean. rotation_hint: Harvest about 21 Sep, which leaves time before every winter crop in the library. Wheat after soybean is supported by an Egyptian trial.
price_card: No Egyptian farm-gate price found (USDA FAS Cairo 2026 gives none). Local output is about 85,000 t, under 2% of demand, so buyers exist; a ministry contract-farming programme is mentioned. FAS says farmers avoid it because of high costs, heat at planting and preferring other crops. An aggregator page's price was NOT used (its yield figure, 0.3 t/ha, is far from FAS's 2.83 t/ha).
